10.MONOCHOROINIC TWINS:
•30% of twins.
•Blastocyst transfer stage in IVF => MC twins.
•80% Bidirectional channels – No complications but risk of IUD.
•Determine Chorionicity @ 11 – 13+6 weeks.
•Not sure => photograph + 2nd opinion.

 

Still not sure =>urgent referral to expert sonologist

•Risk of 2nd loss + neurodevelopmental morbidity.

DS Screening

•1st combined
•2nd trimester quadruple.

Anomaly scan:

@ 18 – 20+6 weeks.

Commonly, Midline structural anomalies in monozygotic twins

⇨Holoprosencephaly.
⇨Heart defects
⇨NTD.

USG 2 weekly from 16 weeks.

@ each USG – Biometry – EFW.

Fetal bladder

DVP. 2 weekly

UA, Doppler UAPI

Complicated MC twining:

⇨All cases managed with FMU

1. TTTS:

•Risk of TTTS is15%
•screening by NT is not recommended
•most commonly due to abnormal AV – Anastomosis.

Symptoms: sudden in abdominal Girth, Breathlessness.

Screening 16 weeks onwards.

Diagnosis: History + USG findings

Severity = Quintero Classification:

Stage I: discordant Amniotic Fluid:

- < 2cm in donor

- > 8cm in recipient

> 10 after 20 weeks

Stage II: Bladder of donor twin not seen.

Stage III: Doppler is abnormal

Arterial changes in donor.

Venous changes in recipient

Stage IV: Hydrops in recipient twin.

Stage V: IUD of 1 or both twins.

Treatment

Before 26 weeks:

laser ablation by Solomon technique

-Follow up: weekly for 2 weeks [ USG (Brain, heart, limb) Doppler, UPAI, MCA PSV]

Then 2 weekly Doppler + Growth.

-S/E: functional heart problems.

After 26 weeks – septostomy/ Amnioreduction.

Delivery: @ 34 – 36+6 weeks.

 

2.SGR:

10 – 15% alone.

50% with TTTS.

•FMU referral: large A – A anastomosis.
•EFW measurement from 20 weeks USG.

Discordance:

Larger Twin – smaller Twin x 100 = Growth Larger twin discordance.

> 20%

Stages of SGR:

Stage I: Growth discordance but positive diastolic flow in both UA.

Stage II: G.D with absent/ Reverse diastolic flow.

Stage III: G.D with cyclical UA diastolic flow.

Positive => absent => reverse.

 

Surveillance:

•2 weekly Doppler.

Delivery:

If growth velocity is (N) & UAD (N)Early onset – poor prognosis => 26 weeks.

Selective reduction by vascular occlusion.

Type I @ 34 – 36weeks.

 

Type II, III @ 32weeks.

•Longer latency than DC twins.
•DV Doppler showing reverse flow or

Abnormal CTG => Consider delivery.

•Risk of unpredictable transfusional events.

 

3.TAPS:

Incidence: 2% alone and 13% in treated

Commonly due to Minuscule A –V anastomosis

Postnatal diagnosis

TTTS Reticulocytosis difference 1.7 or

Hb difference > 8 g/dl

Screening after treatment of TTTS and SGR

17% risk of TAPS after laser of TTTS, Solomon technique risk of TAPS (3%).

serial monitoring by MCA – PSV

* Treatment outcome poorly established.

 

4.TRAP
•1%
•Due to large A –A anastomosis.
5.Discordant Abnormalities:

Urgent referral to FMU, for Karyotyping.

Meticulous mapping before invasive testing.

Sample both sac unless Chorionicity determined before 14 weeks.

Selective Feticide by cord ablation method

DIC monitoring not recommended.

.

 

6.Single intrauterine death: sIUD
⇨Anemia in surviving twin
⇨dIUD – 15%.
⇨Neurological problems in surviving twin 25%.

urgent referral to FMU.

•MRI after 4 weeks of demise of co – twin => to rule out neurological problems.
•MCA PSV – Doppler after demise of co – Twin =>to rule out Anemia of co – Twin.

Uncomplicated MC Twins: delivery 36 – 38 weeks = elective birth.

Monochorionic monoamniotic: 32 – 34 weeks = elective CS.

Risk of Cord entanglement.

Higher order Multiple:

Selective feticide including triplets.

7.Conjoined Twins:

FMU, MDT management

•1/90,000 to 1/100,000 pregnancies.
•Survival 25% I/U demise 10%.
